methodological_rigor.justification: Large-scale retrospective cohort analysis (N=54,185) using standardized comprehensive genomic profiling (F1CDx, 324 genes) with structured data from Japan's national C-CAT database. Proper multivariable Cox proportional hazards modeling adjusted for sex and age. Appropriate survival analysis methodology and time-dependent ROC. Limitations: retrospective analysis without randomization; post-CGP treatment regimens available for only 28.5% of patients; selection bias toward treated patients may inflate efficacy estimates.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Large observational cohort study evaluating clinical utility of CGP-guided biomarker stratification in 54,185 advanced cancer patients across 81 tumor types. Demonstrates 16.6% with level A evidence alterations predict improved OS; only 8% receive CGP-guided approved therapies. Provides real-world evidence on underutilization of genomic testing results and identifies tumor-agnostic biomarkers (TMB ≥20 with pembrolizumab). Directly informs precision oncology implementation decisions.

reporting_quality.justification: Methods section comprehensive regarding data sources, CGP testing platform, evidence classification criteria, and statistical approach. Results well-organized by evidence level, tumor type, and biomarkers. Limitations acknowledged regarding post-CGP treatment data completeness. Data availability limited: pseudonymized registry data with restricted access per C-CAT governance; code mentioned as available in GitHub but methods not fully reproducible without direct C-CAT access.

novelty_literature.justification: First large-scale nationwide analysis of CGP utility in real-world precision oncology practice, evaluating 54,185 unselected patients across 81 tumor types. Identifies treatment landscape gaps with substantial inter-tumor heterogeneity (thyroid/lung >20% receive biomarker-matched therapies vs <2% pancreatic/liver). Tumor-agnostic TMB analysis across cancers and extramammary Paget's disease resistance to pembrolizumab represent novel clinical insights.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-structured manuscript with clear Methods, Results organized by evidence-level and tumor-specific analyses. Extended data figures effectively communicate distributions and survival curves. Discussion appropriately contextualizes gaps between genomic evidence and treatment utilization. However, substantial technical density in methods (genotyping, demultiplexing protocols) may limit accessibility to clinicians.

key_strengths: Large real-world cohort (54,185 patients) with nationwide representation in Japan, providing real-world utility insights beyond randomized trials

Comprehensive analysis across 81 tumor types with tumor-specific stratification revealing substantial practice heterogeneity: therapies utilized in >20% of thyroid/lung but <2% of pancreatic/liver cancers
Tumor-agnostic biomarker validation: TMB ≥20 predicts better OS with pembrolizumab across tumor types independent of MSI status
Prognostic stratification by evidence level (A-E) demonstrates independent OS association with level A alterations after multivariable adjustment for age/sex
Identifies actionable clinical gap: only 8% of patients with actionable alterations receive guideline-matched therapies despite CGP results
key_concerns: Retrospective analysis with 28.5% availability of post-CGP treatment data; missing treatment information introduces potential selection bias and limits generalizability of efficacy estimates
Survival analysis restricted to 87.4% with available data; survival follow-up varies by treatment group (median 18.9 months), potentially confounding OS estimates
No adjustment for multiple comparisons despite numerous statistical tests across evidence levels, tumor types, and biomarkers; inflates type I error risk

Treatment biomarker-response attribution imprecise: BOR data available for only 58.4% of active treatment recipients; cross-trial PFS comparisons (NTRK fusion analysis) limited by methodologic differences
Disparities in treatment utilization may reflect clinical appropriateness rather than undertreatment; unclear how many patients with actionable alterations had contraindications
chief_reviewer.rationale: Tier 3 appropriate for large real-world observational study identifying important precision oncology implementation gaps and validating tumor-agnostic biomarkers, but retrospective design with incomplete post-treatment data and lack of multiplicity correction prevent Tier 2. Suitable for Cancers or European Journal of Cancer with revisions on treatment completeness and statistical adjustment.
